Algeciras (порт лоцоде ESALG) is a major ferry port and city in Spain's Cadiz Province in Andalusia (autonomous region) with population around 120,000 (metro around 270,000). Algeciras is just approx 20 km (12 mi) northeast of Tarifa (on Costa de la Luz), ranked as one of the world's best windsports destinations. The road distance between Algeciras and Cadiz is ~110 km (68 mi) via A381 Highway. The road distance to Gibraltar UK is ~30 km (19 mi) via A7 Highway.

Puerto Algeciras is ranked one of Europe's largest ports by the number of annually handled container ships, cargoes and transhipments. The port's businesses serve commercial shipping (TEU-containers, various cargoes), commercial fishing, passenger shipping (mainly via ferries, also cruise shipping), bunker fueling.

Algeciras benefits from its strategic location (near Gibraltar Strait) and, by annual transshipment volume,s is amongst the world's busiest.

Port facilities are located in Algeciras as well as in other towns part of the metro region (including San Roque, Los Barrios, Tarifa).

In FY2015, by cargo shipping volumes (~100 million tons), Port Algeciras was ranked Spain's and the Mediterranean's largest. By container shipping volumes (2.8 million TEUs in 2010), the port is ranked the world's 31st-largest.

Daily scheduled ferry connections link Algeciras with Ceuta (Spanish Morocco) and Tangier Med (Morocco). These routes are operated by the companies BALEARIA, TRASMEDITERRANEA, FRS (Forde Reederei Seetouristik/Fast Reliable Seaways).

  • Algeciras-Ceuta ferry travel time is ~1 hour, provided by BALEARIA (7 daily crossings), TRASMEDITERRANEA (3 daily), FRS (4 daily).
  • Algeciras-Tangier ferry travel time is 1,5 hours (by BALEARIA /1 daily crossing) and 0,5 hours (by TRASMEDITERRANEA/1 daily).

Algeciras is also an industrial city, has a well-developed fishing industry, and from here are exported various regionally-farmed agricultural products (cereals, tobacco) and livestock. The tourism industry is also growing, with popular day tours from Algeciras to Tarifa and Gibraltar, and also scenic boat cruises in the Bay of Gibraltar.

Algeciras is the terminus of two major European highways going via France and England all the way to Scotland - E05 (ends in Greenock) and E15 (in Inverness). Spanish highways serving the city include Autopista AP-7 (Autopista del Mediterraneo/tall motorway along Spain's Mediterranean coast/La Jonquera-Algeciras), Autovia A-48 (Cadiz-Algeciras), N-340 (Cadiz-Barcelona) and GR-7 (links Spain with Andorra and France).

The nearest airports are in Gibraltar (20 km / 12 mi), Jerez de la Frontera (100 km / 62 mi) and Malaga (120 km / 75 mi).

At a Glance

Independent with some planning or transport. Central Algeciras is compact and suitable for a short walk, but cruise calls are uncommon and ships may use different berths within this large commercial port. Confirm the passenger exit and any shuttle arrangements on board. Gibraltar, beaches and nature areas require transport.

Getting from the Cruise Port

Algeciras is primarily a ferry, cargo and container port rather than a purpose-built cruise destination. Walking inside operational areas may be restricted, so use any shuttle or designated passenger route provided for the call.

From the public port or maritime-station area, Plaza Alta and the central shopping streets are approximately 1 km (0.6 mi) away. The intercity bus station on Calle San Bernardo is also close to the center. Taxis are the simplest option for Getares Beach, Parque del Centenario and Gibraltar.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Explore Central Algeciras

Allow 2–3 hours for Plaza Alta, the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Palma, the small Sanctuary of Nuestra Señora de Europa, the Town Hall and Mercado Ingeniero Torroja. The center is lively and local rather than heavily touristic, with cafés and shops along the pedestrian streets.

This is the easiest independent option, particularly for a short call or when the exact port exit is not known in advance.

Visit Gibraltar

Allow at least 5–7 hours. Gibraltar is roughly 25–30 km (15.5–18.6 mi) from Algeciras by road. Public buses run from Algeciras to La Línea de la Concepción, normally taking about 45 minutes; passengers then walk across the international border into Gibraltar.

A taxi, private transfer or organized excursion is more practical when time is limited. Border queues, traffic and the additional journey from the frontier to Gibraltar’s main sights can substantially lengthen the outing. Carry the travel documents required for both Spain and Gibraltar and verify current entry requirements before leaving the ship.

Organized excursion recommended for visits combining the Upper Rock, viewpoints and central Gibraltar, especially on a call shorter than eight hours.

Relax at Getares Beach

Getares is a semi-urban sandy beach approximately 5 km (3.1 mi) south of central Algeciras. It has a promenade and places to eat, with views toward the Strait and Gibraltar. Allow 3–4 hours including transport.

A taxi is the most convenient choice for cruise visitors. Walking from the port is too time-consuming for an ordinary call. Swimming conditions and beach facilities are seasonal, and exposed weather can make a beach visit less appealing.

Parque del Centenario and Strait Views

This coastal park offers viewpoints over Algeciras Bay, the Strait of Gibraltar and, in clear weather, the North African coast. Paths cross uneven and occasionally sloping ground, so suitable footwear is useful. Combine it with Getares or the nearby coast on a taxi outing of approximately 2–3 hours.

Independent with transport. Arrange a return taxi or confirm local transport before setting out, as the park is not a practical walk from most port exits.

Self-Guided City Walk

Port to Plaza Alta and San Isidro

Distance: approximately 2.5 km (1.6 mi) as a circuit from the public port area
Pure walking time: about 35–45 minutes
Recommended time: 2–3 hours with stops
Difficulty: Easy to moderate; mostly urban streets, with an incline toward San Isidro

  1. Passenger exit or shuttle drop-off: Follow the designated route out of the operational port.
  2. Mercado Ingeniero Torroja: Visit the distinctive circular market when it is open and browse the surrounding produce and food stalls.
  3. Plaza Alta: Pause in the tiled central square beside the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Palma.
  4. Sanctuary of Nuestra Señora de Europa: See the small chapel on the edge of Plaza Alta.
  5. Town Hall: Continue along the central streets to the municipal building.
  6. San Isidro: Walk uphill through this traditional neighborhood of narrow lanes and whitewashed houses.
  7. Parque María Cristina: Descend toward the city park before returning through the commercial center.

Return directly to the confirmed shuttle point or passenger entrance. Do not attempt to re-enter the port through an unauthorized gate.

Nature and Longer Excursions

The surrounding area includes the Río de la Miel, Garganta del Capitán and coastal trails within the Strait and Los Alcornocales natural environments. These are better suited to a guided excursion or prearranged taxi because trailheads lie outside the center and return transport may be difficult to obtain.

Tarifa is another possible excursion destination, approximately 20–25 km (12.4–15.5 mi) southwest of Algeciras. Its old town, Atlantic beaches and Strait views can fit a longer call, but an organized tour or private transfer is preferable to relying on connecting public transport.

Practical Tips

  • Check the ship’s berth, passenger exit and shuttle information before going ashore.
  • Choose central Algeciras for a short or uncertain call; Gibraltar requires substantially more time.
  • Verify opening times locally, particularly for the market, churches, museums and the Paco de Lucía interpretation center.
  • Allow additional time for traffic and border formalities when visiting Gibraltar.
  • For independent trips outside the center, plan the return journey before departure and keep a generous margin before all-aboard time.
